sections.h2: Where is West Haven and what are its neighborhoods?
sections.html:
West Haven is a city in New Haven County on the coast of Long Island Sound, with 55,584 residents in the 2020 census. It covers 10.92 square miles, or about 5,171 people per square mile.

The Oyster River separates it from Milford on the southwest. Orange lies to the northwest, New Haven to the north, and the West River runs along the northeast edge. New Haven Harbor is to the east and the Sound to the south.

  • Center, around the green and Campbell Avenue, the main commercial street.
  • West Shore, along the water.
  • Allingtown, the hilly district that holds the University of New Haven.
  • Sandy Point, a beach and bird sanctuary that extends into New Haven Harbor.

The city has 3.5 miles of publicly accessible beach, which Wikipedia says is about a quarter of the public beach in Connecticut. For a seller, location in one of these areas shapes the likely buyer, and houses near the water are a different product from a hillside house in Allingtown.

sections.h2: What is the history behind West Haven's housing?
sections.html:
West Haven was settled in 1648 as West Farms, part of the New Haven Colony, and became a separate parish in 1719. It split from Orange to become its own town in 1921 and was incorporated as a city in 1961, which is why it calls itself Connecticut's youngest city.

Savin Rock was a seaside resort by the 1870s and later an amusement park that closed in the 1960s. A long redevelopment fight followed, and the area is now parks and shoreline open space under a conservation easement signed in 2007.

The city grew from 25,808 residents in 1930 to 43,002 in 1960 and 52,851 in 1970. Houses from those decades are now old enough that roofs, wiring and heating systems are fair questions for any buyer.

sections.h2: Who assesses and bills property tax in West Haven?
sections.html:
The Assessor's Office values property, and the Tax Collector bills and collects. The Assessor's Office is in City Hall at 355 Main Street, 1st floor, and can be reached at 203-937-3515. Hours are Monday to Friday from 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

ItemWhat the Assessor's page states
Assessment level70% of fair market value
Last revaluation notedRevaluation 2024
Appeal bodyBoard of Assessment Appeals, with a posted legal notice for April 2026
Forms offeredBoard of Assessment Appeals application and representative form
Relief programsState elderly and totally disabled programs, veterans exemptions, blind exemption, renters rebate
RecordsOnline assessment records and West Haven GIS

The Assessor's page also posts a mill rates sheet and a street list by fire district. See the Assessor's Office page for the current files.

sections.h2: Why does the fire district on your street matter?
sections.html:
In West Haven, some of the tax bill can depend on which fire district a street is in. Wikipedia reports that the Allingtown district was folded into the city and that the two remaining independent districts, First Fire Taxation (Center) and West Shore, each levy their own tax rate.

The Assessor's page offers a street list by fire district, and the mill rates are posted as a separate sheet. To estimate a payoff, ask the Tax Collector which district and rates apply to the exact address and whether a district bill is separate from the city bill.

The same article says the state's Municipal Accountability Review Board is providing financial support and guidance to the city, and that residents expect efforts to consolidate the districts. Ask the office whether any change affects the bill you receive.

sections.h2: What are the West Haven tax due dates?
sections.html:
The Tax Collector's office will give you the exact due dates, late-payment interest and the balance on your parcel.

Ask for these items in writing before you sign a sale agreement:

  • the balance of real estate tax on the parcel, including any fire district amount;
  • the date each installment is due and what is already paid;
  • any sewer or other charge that sits on the property record;
  • the last day a payoff figure is good, so the closing date does not strand a few days of interest.

If your home was revalued in 2024 and the bill rose, the Assessor's page links to Revaluation Questions and Answers, and the vendor's taxpayer information site is listed as well.

sections.h2: What does the state require when a West Haven house is sold?
sections.html:
The seller files Connecticut Form OP-236 when the deed is recorded, and the state tax is due when the price is $2,000 or more unless an exemption applies. West Haven's town code on the state form is 156.

  • The grantor, the grantor's attorney or an authorized agent files the return.
  • Participating towns can use the state's myCTREC portal, and the payment is drawn only after recording.
  • Towns that do not take electronic filing receive both pages of the form and a check to the Commissioner of Revenue Services.

The state also lists an exemption for a principal residence sold for too little to pay the mortgages plus the real estate tax and other liens ahead of them, and another for a principal residence deeded in lieu of foreclosure. Your closing attorney should pick the right code. The DRS conveyance tax page lists all of them.

sections.h2: Who works in West Haven and what changed in the local economy?
sections.html:
West Haven was a shipping and manufacturing city, with buckle shops in the Civil War era, Armstrong Rubber in World War II and later Coleco and Sikorsky operations. Bayer closed its plant in 2006, affecting about 1,000 workers, and Yale bought the 137-acre campus in 2007 for life sciences research.

Today the University of New Haven, a U.S. Veterans Affairs hospital and Yale's athletic fields and West Campus are part of the picture. The city's 2020 median household income was $73,566, and it had 22,735 housing units, 5.8% of them vacant. Wikipedia does not list a current top-employer table, so we do not rank employers here.

sections.h2: How do roads, transit and schools affect a West Haven sale?
sections.html:
Interstate 95, Route 34 and U.S. Route 1 run through West Haven, along with Routes 162 and 122. The Connecticut DOT opened a Metro-North station on the New Haven Line in 2013, with 660 parking spaces. Amtrak does not stop in West Haven, and the closest stop is New Haven's Union Station.

CT Transit New Haven buses serve Campbell Avenue and the shore. Tweed New Haven Regional Airport is the nearest airport with air service. The public school system has one high school, a middle school, an intermediate school and six elementary schools.

A cash buyer looks at condition, title and tax status as well as location.

faqs.q: Who do I call about West Haven property assessment?
faqs.a: Call the Assessor's Office at 203-937-3515. It is on the first floor of City Hall at 355 Main Street and is open Monday to Friday from 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

faqs.q: What percent of value does West Haven assess?
faqs.a: The Assessor's page says property is assessed at 70% of fair market value. The last revaluation it notes is Revaluation 2024.

faqs.q: Where do I appeal a West Haven assessment?
faqs.a: Appeals go to the Board of Assessment Appeals, and the Assessor's page offers an application and a representative form. Ask the Assessor's Office for the current filing window.

faqs.q: Does a fire district add to a West Haven tax bill?
faqs.a: It can. Wikipedia reports that the two remaining independent fire districts each levy their own rate, and the Assessor posts a street list by fire district. Ask the Tax Collector which applies to your address.

faqs.q: Can I sell a West Haven house that owes property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Get a written payoff from the Tax Collector, and the title company can pay the tax from the sale proceeds at closing.
